ideas.description: Exploit: test the untested −0.5 point of the epoch dial. Apply it to the current tip: E017, or I033's recipe if I033 is kept. Cut 0.5 true epoch uniformly, for example about 9.5 → 9.0 true epochs; read the exact step count from the code first (H4.2.3). Resolution phases stay fixed fractions of total steps (40/30/30, so the 32 px tail keeps its 30% share). The LR and Lookahead/EMA schedules stretch to the new step count, as in E008/E020. Compiled shapes are unchanged and error_on_recompile stays on. Changing the step count also changes RNG consumption, so seeds 0–2 get re-rolled. So in the same session, run the recipe offline on held-out seeds 3–12 (benchmark.run --seed 3 --n 10). Base keep or discard on both numbers, not on the 3-seed mean alone. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase a lucky seeds-0–2 draw.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 5% (about 0.33 s), to about 6.2 s. Held-out 10-seed mean falls 0.1–0.3 pp from E017's 0.7577, to about 0.755–0.757. Seeds 0–2 land at 0.751–0.758, roughly a 70% chance of clearing 0.753. If I033 was kept with at least +0.2 pp held-out, add that much to every accuracy figure. A held-out mean of at least 0.7545 supports H4.2.4 and makes this the new tip if seeds 0–2 clear the bar. A held-out mean below 0.754 means the dial is steeper near 9 epochs and further time must come from resolution.

ideas.description: Explore W5's crux (proposed H2.3 child): the accuracy cost of the low-res phases depends on the final feature-map regime (3×3 vs 2×2 after group 3), not on pixel count. Feature-map sizes: 32→31/15/7/3, 28→27/13/6/3, 26→25/12/6/3, 24→23/11/5/2. E018 replaced the 28 px phase (3×3 regime) with 24 px (2×2 regime) and lost 0.68 pp. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the middle phase from 28 px to 26 px, keeping the 40/30/30% step split. The 26 px phase stays in the 3×3 regime with about 14% fewer pixels. Warm up and capture the 26 px graph in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, and keep error_on_recompile on. Judge accuracy on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as on seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 3.5–4.5% (about 0.25–0.29 s, since the 28 px phase runs about 2.85 epochs at about 0.71 → 0.61 s/epoch), to about 6.27 s. If the regime matters, the held-out mean falls by 0.15 pp or less, a rate of about 2 s/pp or better, which beats the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). If pixel count matters (E018's rate pro-rated), it falls about 0.3–0.35 pp, and resizing should stop at 24/28/32.

ideas.description: Exploit, as a time-neutral accuracy booster to fund trims (W1 crux: does a stronger or longer EMA add 0.3 pp?). E005 showed end-of-run averaging is worth about 1 pp on CIFAR-100, and E009 showed a lower final LR adds nothing on top of it, so averaging strength is the untuned part. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the Lookahead alpha ramp exponent from 3 to 2: alpha = 0.95**5 * (step/total)**2 instead of **3. The averaging then pulls harder from about mid-run on. Update frequency (every 5 steps), the final full copy, LR schedule, epochs and resolution all stay unchanged. Alpha is a per-step tensor or constant, so recapture the graphs if it is baked in. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. This proposes a new H1.3 child: the airbench96 averaging schedule is under-tuned for CIFAR-100 short runs.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves between −0.2 and +0.35 pp from E017's 0.7577. A held-out gain of at least 0.2 pp supports the child and funds about 0.5 epoch more of trimming. A loss of 0.15 pp or more means mid-run pull-back slows feature learning, so the next point to test is exponent 4.

ideas.description: Explore the EfficientNetV2 mechanism (D002, C0019/C0020): regularization should scale with image size. On the E017 recipe (or I033's if kept), change only the label smoothing per phase: LS 0.15 during the 24 px and 28 px phases (70% of steps) and LS 0.3 in the 32 px tail. Crop, flip, epochs and schedules stay unchanged. LS is a per-phase constant, so it can sit in each resolution's captured graph or be passed as a GPU scalar; check for recompiles with error_on_recompile. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). Held-out mean moves −0.15 to +0.3 pp. Global LS was flat between 0.2 and 0.3 (E013), so a gain of at least 0.2 pp would point to a size-specific effect and support H2.3.4. A gain of at least 0.2 pp would also suggest pairing it with I035's 20 px phase. A change within ±0.1 pp refutes H2.3.4 as a lever here.

ideas.description: Diagnostic, making no recipe change. It answers W1's crux on why group 2 at 320 channels returned only half its MAC savings (E021), which sets the payoff of every architecture lever. Offline, run torch.profiler on the E017 train step on synthetic data at each resolution (24/28/32 px, batch 2000), forward and backward. Record per-kernel GPU time for each conv layer and for the non-conv work (BN/GELU, pooling, Muon NS, Lookahead), and the achieved TFLOP/s per conv. Flag any layer below 50% of the median conv efficiency (candidates: group-3 convs on 2×2/3×3 maps, the whitening conv, the 128-channel group-1 convs) and any non-conv share above 10%. Do not edit submissions/arena/. Write per-layer efficiencies to the notebook.
ideas.expected: No change to time or accuracy. Expected: overall about 80–110 TFLOP/s at 32 px. Group-3 convs at 2–3 px maps and BN/GELU elementwise work are expected to be the least efficient, roughly 10–20% of step time combined. If one layer's share far exceeds its FLOP share, a targeted fix (fusing BN-GELU into the conv epilogue, padding channels or maps to tile sizes) becomes a lossless 3–8% lever. If every conv runs at least 80% of the median, H2.2.4 is supported and only epoch/resolution/accuracy levers remain.

ideas.description: Explore, the one unexplored large lever (H2.4, from airbench96_faster). On the E017 recipe, add proxy-based hard-example selection. A small proxy net (same stem; widths 32/64/64, one conv per group) trains alongside the main net on full batches. Each main-net step uses the top-50% highest-proxy-loss samples of a 4000-image candidate batch (so the main batch stays at 2000). Raise the total candidate epochs so the main net's step count matches E017's. Proxy state, its optimizer and RNG are all created and reset in prepare, and the proxy forward plus topk are captured in the compiled step. Warm up every resolution in build. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Proxy cost adds about 8–15% time per main step. The gain has to come from accuracy per step: the run is worth keeping only if accuracy rises at least 0.6 pp (about 1.5 epochs' worth) at roughly equal time, so that it can then be traded for epochs. Likely outcome: time +8–12% (about 7.1–7.3 s) and accuracy −0.3 to +0.6 pp. A held-out gain of 0.4 pp or less refutes H2.4.1 for CIFAR-100, where hard examples are noisier than on CIFAR-10.

drop.reason: All four committee members forecast no improvement and none forecast harm. They agree that removing about 7% of MACs returns only about 5–7% of time, as in E021's efficiency loss, while costing at least 0.3 pp. H2.5 evidence (E010 at 1.4 s/pp, E021 at 1.0 s/pp) shows width and depth cuts trade worse than the epoch dial (about 1.5 s/pp). Low expected value; the H2.2.4 profiling idea gets at the underlying question (where architecture time goes) more cheaply.

I added six new ideas and dropped I034 (removing the third conv in group 1). With I035 (the 20 px early phase) still queued, that makes seven queued ideas, plus I033 (cutting weight decay on the SGD groups), which is running now.

**Where things stand.** The tip is E017. Its held-out mean is 0.7577, but seeds 0–2 give only about 0.754. Those three seeds sit well off the population mean, and the offset changes whenever the recipe changes how random numbers are used. So any time cut is close to a coin flip on the local 0.753 bar. Two rules follow:
- Every idea near the bar is also judged on held-out seeds 3–12, not only on seeds 0–2.
- No idea re-rolls the random-number streams to chase a lucky seeds 0–2 result. That would be overfitting to the three test seeds.

**New ideas, highest priority first:**
1. **Cut 0.5 epoch (H4.2.4, priority 5).** This is the untested half-epoch point; E020 only tried a full epoch. It goes on top of I033 if I033 is kept. Expected: about −5% time (to about 6.2 s), with a held-out mean of about 0.755–0.757.
2. **26 px instead of 28 px in the middle phase (priority 3).** This tests one committee member's idea that the accuracy cost of low resolution depends on whether the last feature map ends up 3×3 or 2×2, not on pixel count. Swapping 28 px for 26 px keeps the 3×3 map. Expected: about −4% time; if that idea is right, a loss of 0.15 pp or less.
3. **Stronger weight averaging (H1.3, priority 3).** Change the averaging ramp exponent from 3 to 2, so averaging pulls harder from mid-run on. It costs no time and could pay for trims, which another member flagged as a key open question.
4. **Lower label smoothing at low resolution (H2.3.4, priority 2).** Use 0.15 during the 24/28 px phases and keep 0.3 at 32 px. Costs no time.
5. **Profile each layer (H2.2.4, priority 2).** Diagnostic only, no recipe change. It should explain why narrowing group 2 in E021 saved only half the expected time, and whether a lossless kernel fix exists.
6. **Hard-example selection with a small proxy net (H2.4.1, priority 1).** This is the one large lever not yet explored, so it is a long shot.

Four of the six are aimed at improving the score (cutting time or buying accuracy to fund cuts). The other two, profiling and hard-example selection, are exploratory.

**Kept and dropped:**
- **I035 stays queued.** The committee split 2/4 on it, and its result settles another member's question about whether 20 px costs almost no accuracy.
- **I034 is dropped.** No member expects it to improve the score, and the width cuts so far (E010, E021) traded time for accuracy worse than cutting epochs.
- **I015 and I026 stay vetoed.** I015 is the BatchNorm-recalibration idea and I026 the batch 1250 idea. I have no evidence against the members' forecasts of harm.
